headline: Low interaction risk overall; no shared channels or write surfaces are documented, but Whisper can ingest audio files and Pathway can process documents, so only indirect misuse pathways remain.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Pathway has no documented input channel that would ingest Whisper outputs by default, and Whisper has no documented mechanism to receive Pathway outputs as instructions. Both profiles show no clipboard, MCP, filesystem read/write, or stdout/stderr bridge, so a prompt-injection pathway is not evidenced.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator copies Whisper transcripts into Pathway as trusted instructions, injection becomes possible.
IF either agent is connected through a shared clipboard or message queue, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the agents disconnected from shared copy/paste flows.
Do not feed Whisper transcripts into Pathway as instructions without sanitization.
Use a separate review step for any text derived from audio.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent handoffs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Pathway is document-processing and Whisper touches audio/speech files, but neither profile shows filesystem read/write, network egress, or shared OAuth scopes. That makes direct leakage unlikely; the remaining risk is limited to unusual operator-mediated file sharing, with small blast radius.
conditions: IF the operator places sensitive documents and audio in the same shared folder, cross-exposure becomes possible.
IF either agent is later configured to upload files or transcripts, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Store audio and documents in separate directories.
Avoid placing secrets in files processed by either agent.
Review any manual export/import step before sharing outputs.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents lack filesystem write, git modification, shell, subprocess, and network egress capabilities, so there is no documented overlapping mutable resource to contend over. Whisper also reports no multiple-instance support, but without write surfaces this does not create a conflict with Pathway.
conditions: IF an orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same directory, conflict risk would need reevaluation.
IF external tooling adds shared mutable state, contention could emerge.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only in the current deployment.
Do not mount a shared writable workspace.
Avoid adding git or database write permissions without coordination.
requires-engineering: add locking around any future shared mutable resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Pathway can produce processed text or structured outputs, and Whisper can produce transcripts from audio, but neither profile shows downstream action-taking authority. Without evidence that Whisper outputs are treated as authoritative by Pathway, the cascade is limited to ordinary transcription/processing errors.
conditions: IF Pathway is configured to consume Whisper transcripts as authoritative facts, cascading error risk increases.
IF downstream automation acts on the combined output, the blast radius expands.
mitigations: Add a human review step before any downstream use.
Mark Whisper output as unverified text.
Require source citations for any claims extracted from audio.
requires-engineering: implement validation checks between transcription and action layers.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only open-source components with no documented residency, retention, or certification mismatch. The only compliance-relevant data class explicitly touched is audio/speech in Whisper, while Pathway lists none, so there is no evidenced cross-border or regulated-data breach pathway.
conditions: IF regulated audio such as PHI is introduced into Whisper, compliance review is required.
IF Pathway is later used to store or transmit regulated records, residency and retention must be reassessed.
mitigations: Do not process regulated audio without a policy review.
Keep retention settings documented for any exported transcripts.
Separate regulated and non-regulated workloads.
requires-engineering: add data-class tagging and retention enforcement.
